title: A rest after the tour and hazy late 1950s
summary: He took a rest after Europe and cannot recall what he did next.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: When you came back from the tour with Sam Price, what were you doing during that stretch between, say, about 1956 and, oh, up into the Sixties, 1965 and '66 and so forth? Who were you playing with? Where were you playing? Did you play much at all? Was it a dry spell for you?
I just remember taking it easy for a while, or something. I don't know what happened.
Yeah. I took a rest. It was a different climate... Everything over there is different. So it's kind of hard on your heart. You've got to take it easy with...
I taken it easy after the tour. I think it was probably about a month or a couple of months in there where I stopped doing anything.
So you stayed home pretty much?
So that's when I... I think I stayed at home and taken a rest for a while.
What I did after that I just can't remember right now. I think I worked someplace, but...
We were talking around '57, '58, the time of, oh, say, the Sputnik, the boycotts in the South, the television shows like Walt Disney, Peter Gunn -- that period in the Popular Culture.
I don't know what the year... I did some stuff with Kathy Chamberlain.
That early? Years ago? Like 1960? She was much too young. She's younger than I am.
Yeah, she's younger than I am. Maybe it wasn't her. Maybe you did some things with another vocalist from time to time?
During that time, she was round about 20, 21, wasn't she?
Well, according to the literature, she was born in 1948, so in 1958 she would have been ten years old. But in 1970, she might have like 22 or something like that.
